chapters.chapter_title: I Have Fried Chicken for Breakfast

questions.text: What do we call the first meal of the day?
questions.discussion: Breakfast is the first meal of the day.

questions.text: It's noon. Tio eats with his classmates during the midday break. Which meal is it?
questions.discussion: The midday meal is lunch.

questions.text: At seven in the evening, Sari sits down for her main evening meal. Which word fits?
questions.discussion: Dinner is the evening meal in Sari's schedule.

questions.text: “I have ___ for breakfast.” Which choice names both a food and a drink?
questions.discussion: Toast is a food and milk is a drink. The other pairs contain two foods or two drinks.

questions.text: Which sentence reports someone's drink at lunch?
questions.discussion: The sentence names the drink, water, and the meal, lunch.

questions.text: Dita says, “I have eggs for breakfast.” What should her partner put in the breakfast column?
questions.discussion: Dita names eggs after have, then tells us the meal.

questions.text: The note says “Lunch: rice and fish.” Which sentence matches?
options: I have rice and fish for breakfast.
I have rice and eggs for lunch.
I have noodles and fish for lunch.
I have rice and fish for lunch.
questions.answer: I have rice and fish for lunch.
questions.discussion: The note lists both rice and fish under lunch.

questions.text: Reno has soup in the evening. Complete his sentence: “I have soup for ___.”
questions.discussion: The evening meal here is dinner.

questions.text: “What do you have for breakfast?” Which answer gives the requested information?
questions.discussion: What asks for the food or drink, so bread and milk answer the question.

questions.text: You want to learn what Maya eats at lunchtime. Which question should you ask her?
options: What do you have for lunch?
What do you have for dinner?
questions.answer: What do you have for lunch?
questions.discussion: What asks about the menu, and for lunch identifies the meal.

questions.text: Ani says, “I have noodles for lunch.” Tell the class about Ani.
questions.discussion: Use has for one other person and keep the meal as lunch.

questions.text: “My brother ___ fried rice for dinner.” Choose the missing word.
questions.discussion: My brother refers to one other person, so use has.

questions.text: Nina and Bima eat together. “They ___ soup for lunch.”
questions.discussion: They refers to two people and takes have.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the words in the right order?
questions.discussion: Start with the subject, then have, the food, and for breakfast.

questions.text: Rani wrote “I have for lunch rice.” Which correction keeps her meaning?
questions.discussion: Rice follows have. For lunch comes after the food.

questions.text: Ben says, “I have rice for lunch. I have noodles for dinner.” What changes?
options: Both the meal and the food.
Neither the meal nor the food.
questions.answer: Both the meal and the food.
questions.discussion: Lunch changes to dinner and rice changes to noodles.

questions.text: Mira has milk at breakfast and at lunch. Which report matches?
options: Mira has milk at both meals.
Mira has milk only at breakfast.
Mira has milk only at lunch.
questions.answer: Mira has milk at both meals.
questions.discussion: Milk is mentioned for breakfast and lunch.

questions.text: Breakfast: bread and milk. Dinner: noodles and water. Which drink is listed for dinner?
questions.discussion: The dinner entry lists water as the drink.

questions.text: “I have tea for breakfast, and water for dinner.” Which part tells you when the speaker has tea?
questions.discussion: For breakfast connects tea with the breakfast meal.

questions.text: What word is missing? “I have fried chicken ___ lunch.”
questions.discussion: For connects what the speaker has with the meal.

questions.text: Ali says, “I have bread for breakfast.” Ana says, “I have eggs for breakfast.” What is the same?
questions.discussion: Both name breakfast, but their foods differ.

questions.text: Dani has rice and soup for lunch. Ema has rice and fish for lunch. What food appears in both lunches?
questions.discussion: Rice appears in both menus.

questions.text: “For lunch, I have soup. I drink orange juice.” Which belongs in the Drinks column?
questions.discussion: The second sentence identifies orange juice as the drink.

questions.text: A survey has two columns: Lunch Food and Lunch Drink. Lia says, “I have noodles and water.” What goes under Lunch Food?
questions.discussion: Noodles are the food. Water belongs in the drink column.

questions.text: Your worksheet has the heading Dinner. Which answer belongs under it?
questions.discussion: Only this statement gives the menu for dinner.

questions.text: Read the note: “Breakfast: eggs. Lunch: soup. Dinner: rice.” Which order follows the day?
questions.discussion: Read the menus in breakfast, lunch, dinner order.

questions.text: Class note: “I have breakfast at Grandma’s house. I have lunch at school. I have dinner at my home.” Which meal is at the speaker’s home?
questions.discussion: The last sentence puts dinner at the speaker’s home.

questions.text: A friend says, “For breakfast I have bread.” How can you check what the friend drinks at that meal?
options: What do you eat for dinner?
What do you drink for breakfast?
Do you have lunch at school?
questions.answer: What do you drink for breakfast?
questions.discussion: Drink asks about the beverage, and breakfast keeps the question on the same meal.

questions.text: Nuri says, “I have soup for lunch.” Which question remains unanswered?
options: What does Nuri drink for lunch?
What food does Nuri have for lunch?
Who says they have soup for lunch?
questions.answer: What does Nuri drink for lunch?
questions.discussion: The note gives the person, food and meal. It does not give a drink.

questions.text: “We have rice for dinner.” Who has rice according to this sentence?
options: the speaker and at least one other person
questions.answer: the speaker and at least one other person
questions.discussion: We includes the speaker and at least one other person.

questions.text: Your group wants to present its meal. Choose the line that gives both menu and meal.
options: We have rice and eggs for lunch.
questions.answer: We have rice and eggs for lunch.
questions.discussion: The line names rice and eggs and identifies lunch.

questions.text: The food label is spelled incorrectly: “bred.” Which spelling should you use?
questions.discussion: Bread is the spelling for roti.

questions.text: A child writes “I have soup for lunch?” as a statement. Which punctuation fits the statement?
questions.discussion: A period ends this complete statement.

questions.text: Teacher: “What does Riko have for dinner?” Note: “Riko, dinner: fish and rice.” Which reply matches?
questions.discussion: He refers to Riko, and the note gives fish and rice.

questions.text: Sinta says, “Today I have eggs for breakfast. Tomorrow I will have bread for breakfast.” What should the class record for today?
questions.discussion: Today refers to the first menu. Bread is for tomorrow.
